chapter: Harlem, the Cotton Club and Duke Ellington
title: Washboard group at fourteen and record dates
summary: Before Duke he played all kinds of groups, then a washboard band at the Onyx Club in New York, and was called for record dates.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Do you remember the late '20s, what you got involved in? You were talking about 1925, now.
There must have been a great improvement, like say between '25 and 1929. You must have --
So the transition from being a kid playing in Long Island to getting with Duke, you must have been playing all the time.
Yeah. I can't remember them now.
Yeah. Do you think that was when you got with, say, the Washboard Serenaders, or a couple of those washboard groups?
I was 14 when I got with a washboard group.
And we played in New York, at the Onyx Club.
And I used to make record dates, and they'd always come for me. They wanted me to play the guitar.
